note: Design round 9, feature emerald (Extra credits from $100 up), the option chosen: em-digits. rows are copied from the design's emerald.json, verbatim (each row is the full HUD of build.cjs: hud4.js MIX.render on the situation's state with the fable-boss option, colour style, left-aligned, with the 1.0.0 frame; the offhand's well, cols 10-13 of the hotbar line, redrawn by the option). The rows have no totem: they were drawn before the totem's round (9b), so they are Hungerbar's with hud.totem off; with it on, each row also has the totem in hotbar slot 5. situations are the design's inputs: state is the engine's state, ctx.stale whether the credits were read from a usage.json more than 15 minutes old. Kamal's picks (picks-r9.json): em-digits.
name: Three digits, then k
optionNote: From $100 the ◆ gives up its spare cell so the count has three: ◆100 to ◆999, then thousands as ◆ 1k to ◆99k, and a yellow ◆99k from $100,000 (the engine's yellow-cap rule). Below $100 nothing changes. When usage.json is old, the count turns grey (#AAAAAA) instead of white.
title: Extra credits from $100 up
intro: The offhand emerald counts your extra credits in dollars, but its well has two cells for the number, like a Minecraft stack count. From $100 up 1.0 shows a yellow 99, so $500 of credits looks like $99. These options make bigger amounts readable in the same four cells.

situations.note: Less than a dollar: 1.0 leaves the well empty (a bare ◆ would read as one emerald).

situations.label: usage.json 2 hours old ($250)
situations.note: The credits were last read 2 hours ago, so the amount may be out of date.
